title: Scan Reading Pack
user: Readers with scanned books or reports who need trustworthy selectable text and an audiobook-ready package while retaining page references to the original scan.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A reader wants scanned philosophy PDFs converted to text for notes and audiobooks; classic OCR makes mistakes and their only good workaround is sending page snippets to ChatGPT.
A PDF-to-Markdown request says image links without extracted image files make the conversion useless when images matter.

recurrence: Extraction must preserve a usable relationship to the source, not merely emit a text blob.
current_workaround: Run conventional OCR, copy pages into a chat model, or create text and images separately with no reliable page mapping.
incumbents_and_gap: OCRmyPDF, Tesseract, Adobe Scan, and PDF-to-Markdown tools extract content, but a compact reader-oriented pack with page anchors, confidence queues, and local audio export is uncommon.
smallest_useful_product: An offline desktop/PWA flow for image-only PDFs: OCR locally, produce Markdown/EPUB-like HTML with page anchors and extracted figures, queue low-confidence lines, and export SSML/plain text.
success_measure: Users correct fewer than 10 lines per 100 pages before exporting a pack and can jump from any text block back to its source page.
constraints: Use local WASM/native OCR; warn users about copyright and private documents; keep original page coordinates; avoid claims of perfect transcription.
why_distinct: The valuable output is a verifiable reading package with source-page traceability, not an opaque AI transcription wrapper.
